QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_37

question.text: The Indian SSE differs from pure 'matchmaking platform' models (e.g., Brazil's BVSA or South Africa's SASIX) because:

answer.text: It excludes NPOs entirely and serves only FPEs.

It will allow trading for equities issued by FPEs, direct listing for NPOs, a full range of standardised funding mechanisms, a reporting standard, and incentives to attract investors — i.e., it is both a place and a set of processes.
It operates exclusively as a donor-NPO directory with no listing or trading function.
It is a pay-to-list platform where both NPOs and FPEs pay annual listing fees of Rs 1 crore.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pp.51-52 of the workbook, the Indian SSE will allow equity trading for FPEs, direct listing for NPOs, a standardised range of funding mechanisms, a reporting standard, and incentives to pull investors onto it. It 'is a set of processes as much as it is a place'. The Trap: Option A is wrong — NPOs are core constituents. Option C reduces the SSE to a directory (matchmaking model). Option D invents a fee structure. Note: The pp.51-52 comparison emphasises that the SSE is simultaneously a venue (place) and a set of standardised processes — this is what distinguishes it from pure matchmaking platforms.
